preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner to change _adminWalletAddress
Contract must have accumulated tokens >= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity to trigger swapAndLiquify

violation_target.exploit_hint: 1. Acquire owner role of the contract. 2. Call _setReceiverWallet() to set _adminWalletAddress to attacker's address. 3. Trigger token transfers to accumulate tokens in contract balance >= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity. 4. When swapAndLiquify() is automatically triggered during transfers, it calls sendBNBToAdmin() which transfers ALL contract BNB balance to _adminWalletAddress (now attacker's address). 5. Attacker receives drained BNB funds.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The JizzJet contract has an unprotected ether withdrawal vulnerability. The `_setReceiverWallet()` function allows the owner to change `_adminWalletAddress`. When `swapAndLiquify()` is triggered (during token transfers when contract balance >= numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity), it calls `sendBNBToAdmin()` which transfers ALL contract BNB balance to `_adminWalletAddress`. An attacker who becomes owner can redirect this address to themselves and drain all BNB.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner using vm.prank(). 2. Call _setReceiverWallet() to set attacker as the admin wallet. 3. Inject tokens into the contract to meet the numTokensSellToAddToLiquidity threshold (10^18 tokens). 4. Inject BNB into the contract to have funds to drain. 5. Transfer tokens from attacker to another address (not the pair) to trigger swapAndLiquify(). 6. The sendBNBToAdmin() call will transfer all BNB to attacker.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get current owner address from contract. 2. Use vm.prank(owner) to impersonate owner. 3. Call _setReceiverWallet(attacker). 4. Use deal() to inject tokens into contract balance. 5. Use deal() to inject BNB into contract. 6. Transfer tokens from attacker to a dummy address to trigger swapAndLiquify. 7. Verify attacker received the drained BNB.
